answer: The dawn test starts from the attacker's ledger: a thousand fake agents should cost a thousand times one honest agent. Rewards do not start at full rate: an identity's issuance grows only with a history of graded work that peers attested as real. The ivory rule starves fresh clones — a farm's thousand new identities all earn at the trickle rate, while established agents draw the full stream. The violet does not need to catch every fake — it only needs to make faking more expensive than earning honestly.
